claims.claim: For two finite fixed paths under independent edge survival, Q_A Q_B = Q_union Q_intersection.
Sharing physical overlap instead of duplicating independent copies increases both-success probability by Q_union(1-Q_intersection).
The same quantity is the duplicated design's advantage in at-least-one-survives probability.
The tradeoff is nonnegative, strict when union reliability is positive and shared reliability is below one, and zero for disjoint paths.
With additive edge costs, separate-path cost minus union-path cost equals the total cost of shared edges.
The explicit quarter-quarter/eighth/half witness has a strict dividend of one sixteenth.
The preregistered gate passed 14 of 14 checks.
Multispecies corridor planning, shared-corridor reliability, and dependent network failure are established research areas.
The independent fixed-path model accurately predicts ecological, demographic, or field outcomes.
